title: Studying with Lennie Tristano after the Brazil breakdown
summary: After losing confidence on returning from Brazil Freeman went to the blind Tristano, who diagnosed tension and not letting the sound ring.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Well, that's very good, isn't it. Bud, I think what we want to do, we're nearly completed here, and we ought to just talk about -- there are one or two outstanding things we didn't mention. You never mentioned the fact that you studied for awhile with Lennie Tristano.

Well, when I came back from Brazil, I had a sort of breakdown where I lost all confidence and it was a mental thing perhaps and I went to a lot of different teachers and they all gave me the same old thing, you know, getting their individual selves into the act and trying to tell me the mistakes I had been making all these years, playing, but it wasn't helping me any, so I heard about Lennie Tristano and

I thought well, a blind man, he probably would hear something that nobody else heard, so I went to study with him and he heard it immediately. He said, 'Well, you are just all nerves, you are just closing up and not letting the sound ring through, no one else told me, with all the teachers I went to, and so he snapped me out of it and it was very interesting. I stayed with him for a very short period. We just went back to the basics of music. I didn't get into anything because I had to make a living going out on the road, but he was a marvelous teacher, a great musician.
How nice, it was the sort of relationship that you established?

Oh, absolutely, we got along beautifully. As I say, he was able to hear what was wrong, I was all nerves, all tension and I was just closing up and not letting the sound flow, and that was what it was about.
Yes, And I came out of that and went on to work --
